Done and independently verified.

## Change

**`src/context.ts:768-784`** — `Context.redirect()`:

```ts
// Multibytes should be encoded
// CR and LF must be percent-encoded to prevent header injection
/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
!/[^\x00-\xFF]/.test(locationString)
  ? locationString.replace(/[\r\n]/g, (char) => (char === '\r' ? '%0D' : '%0A'))
  : encodeURI(locationString)
/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
```

Behavior:
| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `/destination\r\nSet-Cookie: x=1` | `Headers.set` throws (`invalid header value`) or injects on lax runtimes | `/destination%0D%0ASet-Cookie: x=1`, no `Set-Cookie` header |
| raw CR or LF alone | same throw/injection risk | `%0D` / `%0A` |
| `https://example.com/%0d%0a` | unchanged | unchanged (no double-encoding) |
| `https://example.com/こんにちは` | `encodeURI` | unchanged, same `encodeURI` |
| valid ASCII/`%xx` URLs | unchanged | unchanged |

The multibyte branch was already safe; the ASCII branch is where raw CR/LF bypassed encoding. `encodeURI` is deliberately not applied unconditionally, since it would re-encode existing `%xx` sequences and break the `unchangedURLString` guarantees.

## Regression tests

**`src/context.test.ts:118-153`**
- raw CRLF injection: asserts `302`, encoded `Location`, and `Set-Cookie` is `null` (`:118-123`)
- raw CR only (`:125-128`), raw LF only (`:130-133`)
- multibyte + CRLF, expected `…%0D%0A` (`:135-140`)
- percent-encoded inputs `%0D%0A`, `%0d%0a`, `?next=%0D%0ASet-Cookie` returned byte-for-byte unchanged (`:142-153`)
- existing redirect tests, including `%hello` and `://`-with-`%xx` cases, untouched
